      "observations": [
        "All 22 changed paths were read. This human-authored patch adds same-server EWS MoveFolder and factors item/folder requests into a generic Rust helper. The dependency version, Cargo source replacement, lockfile and checksum change together. Vendored type/test changes are dependency evidence, not Thunderbird-owned style examples.",
        "FoldersOnSameServer compares actual incoming-server objects. The historical folder path selects remote move only for same-server isMoveFolder; other cases retain FolderCopyHandler. The historical success callback expects exactly one new ID, then locally reparents and updates EWS ID before notifying completion.",
        "The historical path discards the return from LocalRenameOrReparentFolder, SetStringProperty and client->MoveFolders; its guard reads rv, so a direct return of NS_ERROR_UNEXPECTED after finding an empty ID does not set that guard value. The accepted source replaces this code with ExchangeFolder and checks local reparent/scheduling results. Do not copy the incomplete historical error propagation.",
        "The selected accepted path handles same-server copy and move separately and treats virtual folders as local. Move retains observed stable descendant IDs; copy syncs hierarchy. That stability statement is explicitly an implementation observation, not a verified protocol specification.",
        "The original test asserts the child leaves parent1 and appears in parent2. It does not directly assert EWS IDs, server state, descendants, callback error handling or cross-server fallback. Current test uses the common copyFolder helper and equivalent local assertions. No tests were executed.",
        "IDL moveFolders originally documents itemIds although its parameter is folderIds and says success of failure. Rust folder wrapper also calls input item_ids, while construct_request uses folder_ids. Scope names to the actual folder contract. New owned JS assertions have nonempty should messages. The two new vendored Rust tests call custom helpers whose actual assert_eq! macros have no message; this is imported test scope only.",
        "Current generic code calls response_into_messages before extracting IDs, but full transport error/partial-success policy and safe listener internals were not expanded here. The fake server emits folderIds even though its filtered result is unused; it does not prove failure handling against a real server.",
        "Complete Bug1956554 description/comments0–2 and D254545 creation-to-final timeline, all18 submitted inline bodies across source phases and footer read. The reported scope is a folder move on the same EWS account, replacing CreateFolder with MoveFolder. External protocol docs, ews-rs PR49 and linked Try/jobs are locators; the author's Good Try Run and build completion notices are historical reports, not a run here.",
        "Actual landing adopts the shared FoldersOnSameServer helper in protocols/common, RefPtr<FolderMoveCallbacks> for the concrete callback, same-server wording in error logging, and the failure folder event in the scope guard. The review's suggested pub(self) becomes pub(super) after the item/folder code is grouped in move_operations. It uses operation_builder and the client/move_operations.rs layout, and documents the request extractor return pair. These are scoped reviewed naming, ownership and module-boundary choices, not global C++/Rust rules.",
        "The requested failure-event notification is present in the guard, but that guard observes its referenced rv. The historical path discards several returned results and returns NS_ERROR_UNEXPECTED directly for an empty source ID without assigning rv, so the done label does not establish complete error propagation. Fixed accepted code has the later ExchangeFolder/listener architecture and checks local reparent/scheduling results. Original IEwsFolderMoveCallbacks and later safe-listener contracts are kept separate.",
        "The reviewer asks whether mock MoveItem only copies. The actual renamed addNewItemOrMoveItemToFolder calls Map.set for the same item ID with a new ItemInfo(destination), replacing that mapping rather than retaining both locations. This verifies the one map update, not all real-server move behavior. The checked MoveFolder fake also discards its filter result when building returned IDs, so it does not demonstrate per-folder failure handling.",
        "Original folder test directly asserts the child leaves parent1 and appears in parent2. Current common helper retains equivalent local assertions and adds separate EWS/Graph tasks. Neither directly asserts remote IDs, descendants, failure callbacks or cross-server fallback. The source comment about stable descendant IDs is explicitly an observation with no known protocol documentation. No test, Exchange request, native store, build, imported Rust test or accessibility path ran."
